59	  `import { chromium } from '/opt/node22/lib/node_modules/playwright/index.mjs'`
60	  (the sibling `index.js` is CJS, so a *named* import from it yields
61	  `undefined`) — or `$(npm root -g)/playwright/index.mjs` if the prefix moved.
62	  Path discovery and its sed-fix-up round-trips cost ~220s across five captured
63	  sessions, every one of them re-deriving the same two facts.
64	- **Keep one browser driver script per session and re-point it.** Authoring a
65	  fresh throwaway Playwright script per screenshot cost 29 heredoc writes and
66	  ~7 minutes of wall clock across the captured sessions (one session alone: 16
67	  writes, 4.5 min). Write the driver once into the scratchpad, take the URL,
68	  selector and output path from `process.argv`, and re-run it — a re-run is
69	  seconds where a rewrite is 15–20s.
70	- To build a `/plan` favourites list for the render, a plain slug-per-line text
71	  file is accepted by the parser — pick shows spanning the statuses (and some
72	  same-day doubles) you want to eyeball.
73	- **Known-noisy console output from the served page.** A page driven off
74	  `python3 -m http.server` reliably logs a `favicon.ico` 404 (the repo ships
75	  none) and often `net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET` as the browser tears down. Neither
76	  is an application error — filter both out of a smoke script's error assertion
77	  so that a red run means something, rather than sending you chasing a phantom
78	  404 through extra browser runs.
79	- To match edfringe.com's live styling (e.g. the ticket-availability colours on
80	  the `/plan` grid), fetch the official site's CSS with `curl` through the agent
81	  proxy and read the palette out of it. `WebFetch` returns rendered text without
82	  the CSS, and headless Chromium cannot tunnel the proxy to reach an external
83	  host — `curl` is the one path that works for off-box assets.
84	
85	## The site is two front-ends — cross-page behaviour goes in `shared/`
86	
87	The Now page (`index.html` + `js/app.js`) and the planner (`plan/` + `plan/plan.js`)
88	are separate front-ends, and `plan/lib/` is the planner's own engine, not a common
89	library. But both are now ES modules, so **anything that must behave the same on
90	both pages belongs in `shared/`** and is imported by each — never copy-pasted.
91	Both pages spell the import the same way (`../shared/geo.js` resolves to
92	`/shared/geo.js` from either), so moving a value there is a small change.
93	
94	What is still genuinely twinned (untangled the same way when next touched): the
95	header `debug v<version>` pill, the Now/Plan nav, and the haversine in
96	`plan/lib/travel.js` that was ported from `js/app.js`.
97	
98	A shared module needs **no** `package.json` to mark it as ESM: the pinned Node 22
99	detects module syntax in a `.js` file by itself, with no warning and no flag, so
100	`node --check` and the test suite both handle it. `plan/package.json` predates
101	that detection and its stated reason (silencing a module-detection warning) no
102	longer applies; it is harmless, so it stays, but do not copy it as a pattern —
103	the `edfringe-no-stray-package-json` check flags any other one.
104	`.js` and `.mjs` are both served as `text/javascript` by `python3 -m http.server`,
105	so the extension is a style choice — use `.js`, matching `plan/lib/`.
106	
107	A new top-level source dir must be added to `scripts/verify.sh`'s `git ls-files`
108	list, or nothing in it is ever parse-checked — the `edfringe-verify-sh-covers-source-dirs`
109	check catches an omission. Note that `git ls-files` only sees *tracked* files, so
110	a new file silently sits outside the syntax sweep until it is committed — the
111	"checked N files" count is not evidence your new file was among them.
112	
113	## `.claudinite/shared/` is generated output — never hand-resolve its conflicts, always take the fresher version
114	
115	## A pack rule or check encodes a *work procedure*, never product behaviour
116	
117	Rules and checks in `.claudinite/local/packs/` are about **how work is done here**
118	— the gate that must stay wired, the tool that must be launched a certain way, the
119	files that must move together. **Product behaviour is not a rule.** What the site
120	does — which ticket statuses count as unavailable, what the Now page shows, how
121	far "walkable" reaches — is a **requirement**, and it belongs in the requirements
122	spec (`product/requirements.md`, the `executable-requirements` pack) and its
123	tests, never in a pack's `rules`.
124	
125	The trap is that product behaviour reads exactly like a good check candidate: it
126	is deterministic, statically detectable, and genuinely worth enforcing, so a
127	prose-to-checks sweep will happily convert it. The 2026-07-30 sweep did: it turned
128	the `ticketStatus`-not-`soldOut` rule into an `edfringe-ticket-status-unavailable`
129	check, with a clean scoped parse and a see-it-fail proof against mutated real repo
130	content — a well-built check of the wrong kind, which the owner rejected on sight
131	("Rules shouldn't be about product requirements, only work procedures"). The
132	sibling conversion in the same PR, `edfringe-normalizer-selftest-in-verify` ("the
133	offline self-test must stay wired into `verify.sh`"), was the right kind and
134	stayed.
135	
136	Apply the test **before** writing the check, since the build quality of the check
137	tells you nothing about whether it belongs: *if the product changed its mind
138	tomorrow, would this rule be wrong?* If yes it is a requirement — a red check
139	would then be reporting a product decision as a process violation, and the
140	requirements spec is where that decision is already supposed to live. If instead
141	it would still hold because it describes how we work regardless of what the
142	product does, it is a rule. Prose in a `RULES.md` gets the same test: the
143	`ticketStatus` paragraph in the `edfringe-data` pack is background a scraper
144	editor needs, not a rule, and it is not convertible.
145

1	# EdFringeNow — the data pipeline (scraper/ and data/)
2	
3	The domain of this pack: getting show data out of edfringe.com and into the
4	committed files the site serves. Read it before touching `scraper/` or anything
5	under `data/`. The API's own field reference lives in
6	[scraper/SCRAPING.md](../../../../scraper/SCRAPING.md) and the file layout in
7	[scraper/README.md](../../../../scraper/README.md) — this is the working
8	judgment those two don't carry.
9	
10	## The live API is unreachable from a session — don't try, and don't fake it
11	
12	`edfringe-tikketr-web-api.equhost.com` is blocked by the sandbox egress proxy and
13	`edfringe.com` returns 403 to `WebFetch`. So: no session — this one included —
14	can verify a scraper change against live data. Anything that must touch the API
15	runs on a GitHub-hosted runner: the `Scrape edfringe shows (full)` workflow
16	(`.github/workflows/scrape.yml`), the `refresh-shows` / `refresh-tickets`
17	scheduled tasks, or the throwaway probe procedure in the `probe-edfringe-api`
18	skill. Never "verify" a scraper change by reasoning about what the API probably
19	returns — either run it on a runner, or say plainly that it is unverified.
20	
21	`python3 scraper/normalize.py --selftest` is the one transform check that runs
22	offline; it exercises raw→master→day-file→`shows.min.json` on a fixture, so a
23	normalizer change is verifiable here even though a fetch change is not. Because
24	it is the only offline verification a scraper change can get, it must stay wired
25	into `scripts/verify.sh` — the `edfringe-normalizer-selftest-in-verify` check
26	enforces that (a step *label* naming the self-test does not count; only a command
27	line does).
28	
29	## `ticketStatus`, never the `soldOut` boolean
30	
31	"Can I get a ticket" comes from the per-performance `ticketStatus`, not the
32	`soldOut` flag: a performance can be `soldOut: false` and still have nothing to
33	sell online (`NO_ALLOCATION_CONTACT_VENUE`). The site treats `SOLD_OUT` and
34	`NO_ALLOCATION_CONTACT_VENUE` as unavailable and everything else as available
35	(`NO_TICKETS_STATUSES` in `js/app.js`), and unknown means available. Any new
36	availability logic — client or scraper — keys off `ticketStatus`; `soldOut` is
37	carried through for display only.
38	
39	## Prices are fetched once, and "unknown" is a third state the encoding must keep
40	
41	`data/prices.json` is a fetch-once cache (`scraper/fetch_prices.py`), off the
42	nightly path: a show's price bands are set when it goes on sale, unlike its
43	ticket status. `refresh-shows` reads the cache and carries the amounts through
44	untouched — it never re-fetches them. So the festival keeps adding shows the
45	cache has never seen, and **a show with no price is a normal, permanent state of
46	the data**, not a gap the pipeline should close.
47	
48	Which means the encoding carries three states, not two, and every stage has to
49	preserve the distinction:
50	
51	| state | master | wire |
52	|---|---|---|
53	| costs nothing | `priceMin: 0` | `pm: 0` |
54	| priced | `priceMin: 22.5` | `pm: 22.5` |
55	| unknown | `priceMin: null` | no `pm` key at all |
56	
57	`priceMin: 0` and `free: true` are **not** the same claim and don't always agree.
58	The flag comes from the listing; the £0 can also come from the price API, which
59	returns a single `Price band 1` at £0.00 for a handful of shows the listing
60	doesn't flag free — pay-what-you-want, or a box office that never set a price
61	(10 of 3,664 in the first full run). Both readings are honest about what a ticket
62	costs, so the price path keys off `priceMin`, and `free` stays what the *listing*
63	said. Don't "fix" one to match the other.
64	
65	Never encode unknown as `0`, and never let a decoder default it to one: a stage
66	that collapses three states into two is lying about money, and nothing
67	downstream can recover the difference. What the site then *does* with an unknown
68	price is a product decision, not a pipeline one — it lives in `shared/price.js`.
69	
70	Two traps in the raw price payload, both already handled and both worth not
71	re-introducing: amounts arrive as **strings**, and nearly every show carries a
72	£0.00 "Personal Assistant" concession (a carer's companion ticket) that must not
73	be read as the cheapest price. See the pricing section of
74	[scraper/SCRAPING.md](../../../../scraper/SCRAPING.md).
75	
76	## The committed data is generated output — regenerate it, never hand-edit it
77	
78	`data/raw_pages/` is a git-ignored regenerable cache. `data/normalized/`,
79	`data/venues.json` and `data/days/` **are** committed, because the browser
80	fetches them — but they are still generator output. Fix the data by fixing
81	`scraper/normalize.py` and re-running it (`--merge` for a top-up, no flag for a
82	full rebuild from the raw cache); a hand-edit is silently overwritten by the next
83	`refresh-shows` run and leaves the bug in the generator.
84	
85	`data/prices.json` is the one exception, and it is an exception to the *direction*
86	rather than the rule: it is committed, but it is normalize.py's **input**, written
87	by `scraper/fetch_prices.py`. Nothing regenerates it on a schedule, so nothing
88	overwrites a hand-edit either — which is precisely why editing it by hand is still
89	wrong: the edit survives, silently disagreeing with the box office forever. Re-run
90	the fetch. The `edfringe-data-dir-is-generator-output` check allows it **by name**,
91	so a second file can't ride in on its shape.
92	
93	## Changing the wire format is a four-file change
94	
95	The day files and `shows.min.json` reference `data/venues.json`'s global lists
96	**by position** (`genre`, `room`, `subs`, `ts`; `g`, `rm`, `sg`, `ar`, `p[].t`).
97	That encoding has one producer and two decoders, and they must move together:
98	
99	- producer — `scraper/normalize.py` (`build_lookups` / `build_day_files` /
100	  `minify_master`)
101	- decoder 1 — `js/app.js` `adaptShow`, for the day files
102	- decoder 2 — `plan/lib/hydrate.js` `rehydrateShows`, the exact inverse of
103	  `minify_master`, round-tripped against the real committed files by
104	  `plan/lib/__tests__/hydrate.test.mjs`
105	
106	Add or drop an indexed field and all three change in the same commit. That the
107	indices still *resolve* is enforced by the `edfringe-lookup-indices` check — it
108	catches a lookup list regenerated without its day files, but nothing can catch a
109	decoder left reading the old key, so check both decoders by hand.
110	
111	The same three-way move applies to plain (non-indexed) wire keys such as the
112	price fields `pm` / `px`, with one extra hazard: the round-trip test compares the
113	rehydrated record to the master **as JSON**, so a new master key has to appear in
114	the *same position* in `normalize_event`'s dict and in `rehydrateShows`'s object
115	literal. Adding it in one place and appending it in the other fails the
116	round-trip on key order alone, which reads as a data bug and isn't one.

5	
6	# Probe the live edfringe API from a session that can't reach it
7	
8	The sandbox egress proxy blocks `equhost.com`, and `edfringe.com` 403s
9	`WebFetch` — so the API is only reachable from an **open-network GitHub Actions
10	runner**. This is the procedure for one-off questions (schema introspection, a
11	single show's payload, the real value set behind an enum). Bulk data is not this
12	skill's job: that is the `Scrape edfringe shows (full)` workflow
13	(`.github/workflows/scrape.yml`) or the `refresh-shows` scheduled task.
14	
15	**First: check whether the answer is already recorded.**
16	`scraper/SCRAPING.md` holds the operations table, the full `EventDetail` field
17	surface, the `attributes[]` bag, and the pricing/`ticketStatus` findings — all of
18	it captured by exactly this procedure. Probing for something already written
19	there burns a runner for nothing.
20	
21	## The procedure
22	
23	1. **Write the probe as a script under `scraper/`** — a few dozen lines, reusing
24	   `fetch_shows.py`'s `get_token` / `fetch_events_page` and its
25	   `DEFAULT_USERNAME` / `DEFAULT_PASSWORD` (the site's public anonymous
26	   credentials) rather than re-deriving auth. Print the answer to stdout; the job
27	   log is your return channel.
28	2. **Add a workflow that runs it on push to your branch**, path-filtered to that
29	   script so it cannot fire on anything else, `permissions: contents: read`, and
30	   `actions/setup-python@v5` (the scraper is stdlib-only — no install step).
31	3. **Push, then read the run's job logs** through the Actions API
32	   (`mcp__github__actions_list` → `mcp__github__get_job_logs`). Iterate on the
33	   query by pushing again; each push is one runner-minute.
34	4. **Record what you learned in `scraper/SCRAPING.md`** — the point of the probe
35	   is that the next session doesn't have to repeat it.
36	5. **Delete the probe script and its workflow before opening the PR.** They are
37	   scaffolding, and a push-triggered workflow left in the tree is a live wire.
38	
39	## Guardrails
40	
41	- **Rate-limit like the real scraper.** `fetch_shows.py` sleeps a random 4–9 s
42	  between requests; a probe that hammers the API from a datacentre IP is how the
43	  anonymous credentials stop working for everyone.
44	- **`performancePrices` is per performance** — there is no bulk price endpoint.
45	  A probe that loops it over a whole day is thousands of calls; sample one show.

---VERIFY---
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# The repo's single verification gate: unit tests, JavaScript parse-checks, and
# Python byte-compilation. Both the pre-commit hook (.githooks/pre-commit) and
# CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) run *this* script, so "green locally" and
# "green on GitHub" mean exactly the same thing.
#
# Fast (well under a second) and dependency-free — everything uses the node /
# python already needed to work on the project.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

step() { printf '\n\033[1m▶ %s\033[0m\n' "$1"; }

step "Unit tests — node --test"
# The shared/ helpers both front-ends import, the Now page's own js/ tests, the
# planner's own tests, plus the local packs' — one glob for each pack's own
# pack.test.mjs (its checks' red-first fixtures), one for the shared task
# declaration test, one for the per-task tests beside each task. Those tests import
# every pack manifest and task declaration, so they are also what parse-checks that
# tree (the syntax sweep below deliberately stays off the .claudinite mount).
# Keep in step with the "test" script in package.json.
node --test shared/__tests__/*.test.mjs js/__tests__/*.test.mjs plan/lib/__tests__/*.test.mjs .claudinite/local/packs/*/*.test.mjs .claudinite/local/packs/edfringe/tasks/*.test.mjs .claudinite/local/packs/edfringe/tasks/*/*.test.mjs

step "JavaScript syntax — node --check"
# Only our own tracked source: the js/ app, the plan/ planner, the shared/
# code both import, and the scripts/ tooling. Never the vendored .claudinite
# mount (not our code) or the plan/design/ mock (HTML).
js_files=$(git ls-files 'js' 'plan' 'scripts' 'shared' | { grep -E '\.m?js$' || true; } | { grep -v '^plan/design/' || true; })
js_count=0
for f in $js_files; do
  node --check "$f"
  js_count=$((js_count + 1))
done
echo "checked ${js_count} JavaScript file(s)"

step "Python syntax — py_compile"
py_files=$(git ls-files 'scraper/*.py')
if [ -z "$py_files" ]; then
  echo "no Python sources found — skipping"
elif command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  python3 -m py_compile $py_files
  echo "checked $(printf '%s\n' $py_files | wc -l | tr -d ' ') Python file(s)"
else
  echo "python3 not installed — skipping (CI always has it)" >&2
fi

step "Normalizer self-test — normalize.py --selftest"
# Exercises the raw→master→day-file→shows.min.json transforms on a fixture (no
# network / no raw data), so the packer and the day-file builder are covered here
# and the round-trip decoder is covered by plan/lib/__tests__/hydrate.test.mjs.
if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  python3 scraper/normalize.py --selftest
else
  echo "python3 not installed — skipping (CI always has it)" >&2
fi

printf '\n\033[32m✓ all checks passed\033[0m\n'

=== .github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml ===
# Claudinite per-repo task scheduler — the repo's ONLY cron
# (per-project-scheduling DESIGN §3). A thin shim: all logic lives in the
# vendored engine, so this file changes rarely (schema and behavior changes ride
# the vendor refresh, not edits here). It runs hourly on a repo-hashed minute
# constrained to :10–:50 — spreading the fleet, dodging GitHub's :00 stampede,
# and staying clear of the hour boundary the slot math anchors on.
#
# The minute below is a placeholder; bootstrap/vendoring rewrites it to this
# repo's stable hashed minute in :10–:50, computed by
# `node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/hash-minute.mjs <owner/repo>`
# (scheduler-workflow-shape enforces the range; baselining re-derives the value to
# catch drift). `workflow_dispatch` allows a manual run; the concurrency group
# serializes runs so a slow run and its successor never overlap.
#
# A manual run may carry `overrides` — ONE free-form `KEY=value` string, because
# GitHub cannot declare arbitrary named inputs. It reaches the engine as
# `CLAUDINITE_OVERRIDES`, and the engine understands exactly one key:
# `FORCE_TASKS=<comma-separated task ids>`.
# It runs those tasks even though their slot has already passed, and
# WITHOUT consulting their preconditions — forcing is the operator's decision, so
# nothing asks the task whether it agrees. The engine learns "run these ids",
# never what any of them do, and no task declaration mentions forcing at all.
name: Claudinite scheduler

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '49 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      overrides:
        description: 'Manual-run overrides: comma-separated KEY=value. FORCE_TASKS=<task ids> runs those tasks unconditionally, even when their slot has passed, e.g. FORCE_TASKS=baselining.'
        required: false
        default: ''

concurrency:
  group: claudinite-scheduler
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write        # read the repo + vendored engine; baselining's deliver() pushes the maintenance branch (agent-preprocessing §7/E4)

## The prose

`edfringe-data/skills/probe-edfringe-api/SKILL.md`, step 5:

> **Delete the probe script and its workflow before opening the PR.** They are scaffolding, and a push-triggered workflow left in the tree is a live wire.

**Gate 1 — a working rule, not a product statement.** Nothing about shows, tickets, venues or what the site renders. If the product changed its mind tomorrow the rule is unchanged: it is scaffolding hygiene for the one procedure that reaches the live API. It is a rule.

**Check-the-world.** Yes — a workflow's own trigger block is a static signature. A push trigger not pinned to the default branch is exactly the shape a leftover probe has.

**Dedupe.** No existing check covers it. `gha/no-scheduled-fleet-executor` is about crons only; the other `gha/*` checks are about checkout, labels, pipefail, secrets, Pages artifacts and branch naming.

## The check

`edfringe-no-branch-push-workflow`, **blocking**, on the **edfringe-data** pack — homed there because the probe procedure is the one thing in this repo that legitimately creates such a workflow, and re-hitting the rate-limited edfringe API from a datacentre IP on every branch push is what makes the residue expensive rather than merely untidy.

12 fixtures, both directions proven by mutation:

Exactly the check module, its `pack.mjs` registration, and its fixtures. Nothing under `.claudinite/shared/` touched; no pack outside `edfringe-data`.
